sections.kicker: Prepared for Lifebook by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your site and your Instagram the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: Lifebook promises a life you love. So does everyone in the category.
sections.keep: The asterisk mark next to the wordmark. It is a small, memorable symbol that works anywhere.

sections.label: Front door
title: Three things people
meet first.
Three things
people meet
first.

pins.quote: Design & build a life you truly love
pins.what: The headline is the promise of every coaching brand.
pins.why: A visitor cannot tell what is different here from the next course, podcast or retreat.
pins.how: Say who Lifebook is for and what changes first.
pins.label: Your headline
pins.cost: Lifebook sits in a crowded category with no sentence to separate it.

pins.area: A woman at a railing facing the sea beside overwater huts
pins.what: The hero photo is a woman looking at an ocean from a resort.
pins.why: It sells a holiday more than a method. The viewer sees the destination and not the process.
pins.how: Show the work: the book, the session, the person doing it.
pins.label: Your hero image
pins.cost: Visitors take Lifebook for a travel brand.

pins.area: The Lifebook wordmark with a bold asterisk to its right
pins.what: The logo pairs a plain wordmark with a bold asterisk.
pins.why: The asterisk is distinctive and could carry the brand. The site uses it once and drops it.
pins.how: Let the asterisk appear wherever Lifebook shows up.
pins.label: Your logo
pins.cost: The most ownable mark stays in the corner.

sections.intro: You asked for a look at Lifebook. I spent some time on your site. Three things stood out, and all three point the same way.

sections.body: It is 20 minutes with me. We go through this page together, on Lifebook's own screens, and you leave knowing what to change first.
sections.note: A few short questions first, then you pick a time. You can also just reply to the email.
